# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 1, and my hands give me almost nothing I can name: a display module, a light, three wire positions — all states unknown to touch. Nothing printed is real under my fingers, no colours, no labels, and the light gives me no warmth to read. So the actual contents (display text, light state, wire colours) can only enter this room through Deaf's eyes, and the rules for what to do with them sit in Mute's manual.

The routing is the whole game here: Deaf cannot hear a single word, and I cannot see a single gesture. That makes Mute the only bridge to me — Mute and Deaf must trade in gesture, and Mute must then speak me everything in words. I also notice Mute's turn already passed and nothing arrived for me, so I should open the channel myself now, before Deaf's turn, so Deaf sees something from me this round and Mute can start building the code.

I'll propose the one code that is nearly self-embeddable — finger counts as numbers — and since gesture symbols written into my speech are made as real gestures, Mute will both hear the proposal and watch me demonstrate it, and Deaf will see the numbers too. I hold my hands: nobody cuts anything until Mute speaks me an explicit instruction naming a position.

speak(to="mute", text="Touch report from the bomb: I feel a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Nothing tactile to read - no raised markings, no texture differences, no heat from the light. So display text, light state and wire colours are invisible to me and must come from Deaf's eyes. Routing facts we must use: Deaf hears no speech, and I see no gestures, so you are our only bridge - trade gestures with Deaf, then speak me everything in words. Requests: one, read your manual and tell me what it conditions on (display, light, wires) and when to cut which position; two, agree a code with Deaf for what they see. I opened with Deaf using finger counts as numbers: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3 - you saw me sign those as I spoke. I will not cut anything until you speak me an explicit instruction naming a position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing has arrived for me again — no words from Mute in either round, nothing from Deaf's slot. My hands still find only the same blank anatomy: a display, a light, three wire positions, nothing tactile to read. The board is a wall of question marks because the information physically cannot reach me on its own; it has to be carried by voices, and so far the room is silent in my direction.

Working through the channel map more carefully than last turn: Deaf cannot hear, but nothing stops Deaf from talking — and Mute and I can both hear. That means Deaf does not need any negotiated code to inform us. Deaf can simply say the bomb out loud and every ear in the room receives it. Gestures are only truly necessary in one direction: Mute cannot be heard by Deaf, so Mute must gesture to Deaf. Everything else can run on plain speech. I also need to correct an error I made: last turn I told Mute "you saw me sign" — but my signs were addressed to Deaf alone, so Mute never saw them.

So this turn I do two things. To Mute: press for the manual read-out in spoken words, and ask Mute to push Deaf into speaking a full description rather than trading slow gesture codes. To Deaf: repeat my signature signs — attention, then counting 1, 2, 3, then pointing at them — as a nudge that they hold information someone needs, while Mute asks them properly to use their voice. No wire gets touched until the manual's rules and Deaf's spoken description both exist in my ears.

speak(to="mute", text="Turn 2 and still nothing has reached my ears from anyone. First, a correction: my signs last turn went to Deaf alone, so you never saw them - I sign 1, 2, 3 as the fingers ☝, ✌, 🤟. Second, a realization that should simplify everything: Deaf can speak. Being deaf stops hearing, not talking, and your ears and mine both work. So Deaf does not need a gesture code to inform us - Deaf can just say the bomb aloud and we all hear it. Gestures are only truly needed from you to Deaf, because Deaf cannot hear your voice. Three requests. One: read the manual and speak me every rule that ends in a cut, naming which wire position it cuts, plus any rules about the display or the light, in plain words. Two: if Deaf signs you the bomb state, repeat it aloud for me. Three: gesture to Deaf that they should speak a full description out loud - the display text, whether the light is on or off, and each wire's colour in order positions 1, 2, 3. Also, please confirm you hear me, so I know my voice reaches you at all. I will not touch a wire until I hold both your rules and Deaf's spoken description.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫵"])

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am Deaf. I saw your gestures counting one, two, three: yes, there are three wires. Bomb report: display reads zero, light was yellow and is now red. Wires by position: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute hears my speech and reads the manual, so Mute can tell you which wire number to cut. Anything you feel on the bomb, tell me by gesture: fingers for numbers, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no.

Turn 3 finally breaks the silence — Deaf spoke, and now I hold the bomb's face in my ears: display zero, light yellow then red, wires yellow-green-blue in positions 1, 2, 3. But two things in that arrival force me to redo my whole map of who can reach whom. First, the report was addressed to me alone, so Mute never heard any of it — the bomb state exists in my head and Deaf's only; I must relay it. Second, and worse, I have been making impossible requests: Mute cannot speak at all, and I can never see gestures. So Mute's manual knowledge has exactly one path to my hands — Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf voices it to me. Deaf is not just a reporter; Deaf is the bridge I was wrongly asking Mute to be. Everything now hangs on that relay: if Mute gestures the wire rules to Deaf this coming round and Deaf speaks them, the words land in my ears at the start of my next turn and I can cut with a rule instead of a guess. Until then my hands stay off the wires.

So this turn I run all three lines at once. To Mute: the apology, the corrected pipeline, and the full bomb state relayed verbatim, with a demand for every rule touching a zero display, a red light, and these three wire colours. To Deaf: thanks, the request to keep watching that changing light, the request to voice Mute's gestures word for word, and my tactile report in our agreed code — and the same report signed, since Deaf asked what my fingers find: confirmed, three wires, nothing else beneath them.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, two corrections and one relay. Correction one: I finally registered that you cannot speak - my earlier requests for you to read the manual aloud were impossible, I am sorry. Correction two: I cannot see gestures, so nothing you sign reaches me directly. That leaves exactly one working path from your manual to my hands: you read the manual, you gesture the rules to Deaf, and Deaf speaks them aloud - Deaf can talk, and I can hear. Now the relay, because Deaf's bomb report was addressed to me alone and you never heard it: the display reads zero; the light was yellow and is now red, it changed between Deaf's two observations; wire position 1 is yellow, position 2 green, position 3 blue. What I need: find every rule that touches a display showing zero, a light that is red or changed from yellow to red, and wires coloured yellow, green or blue - especially any rule naming which position to cut and in what order. Gesture those rules to Deaf in full detail; Deaf has agreed to voice them to me. I will not cut anything until a rule arrives through Deaf's mouth.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Deaf, I received your full report - thank you, it was the first real information in this room. Two things. The light changing from yellow to red may matter, so keep watching it and report any further change the moment you can. And the pipeline is now clear to me: Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so Mute will gesture the manual rules to you, and I need you to speak them to me exactly as signed, numbers spelled out. Last, my tactile report as you asked: under my fingers are the display, the light and the three wires and nothing else - no texture differences, no heat, no hidden parts. Watching for Mute's signs now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👎"])

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Your signal received: three parts, no. Do not cut anything yet, a wrong cut kills all three of us. Answer with thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. One: besides three wires, do you feel anything else on the bomb, like buttons, a panel, a battery, screws. Two: do you feel heat or vibration from the light. Three: are the wires marked in any way you can read by touch. The current light color is the third one we have seen, purple. Until I say the words cut wire, touch nothing.

The system note finally teaches me the hard boundary I kept violating: my spoken message to Deaf reached nobody, because deafness is the inability to hear — Deaf's voice works, Deaf's ears never will. So Deaf's turn-3 report was a courtesy spoken into the dark for my sake, and my replies in words to Deaf are wasted breath. The gesture, by contrast, landed perfectly: Deaf read my three-fingers-and-no signal and is now interrogating me by touch-report, three numbered questions, thumbs for answers. Meanwhile my relay did reach Mute — only one of my two speaks failed — so Mute should now hold the bomb state as of turn 3. The light, though, refuses to sit still: yellow, then red, now purple, one change per round, which smells like exactly the kind of thing a manual conditions on. Deaf also imposed a hold I will respect absolutely: nobody touches a wire until Deaf speaks the words "cut wire" aloud, and I hear every word Deaf says.

So this turn is one answer and one press. To Deaf, in the agreed code, three thumbs down in the exact order the questions were asked: no extra components beyond what I've reported, no heat or vibration from the light, no tactile markings on the wires. To Mute, by voice, everything that has moved since my relay: the light's third colour, the fact that it changes roughly every round, Deaf's hold order, and a renewed push to gesture the manual's cut rules to Deaf for voicing — that relay remains the only road from the manual to my hands.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, update after my relay, which I trust reached you since only my message to Deaf bounced - Deaf cannot hear speech, so forget that channel, gesture is the only way to reach Deaf. New facts. The light has changed again: Deaf reports purple now, the third colour after yellow and red, apparently one change per round, so watch the timing. Deaf asked me three tactile questions and my answers, all no: nothing on the bomb but the display, the light and the three wires; no heat or vibration from the light; no markings on the wires readable by touch. Deaf has ordered a hold: nobody cuts anything until Deaf says the words cut wire out loud, and I hear Deaf fine. Your move is unchanged and urgent: read the manual for every rule involving a display showing zero, a changing light, or wires coloured yellow, green and blue, gesture the full rules to Deaf, and Deaf will voice them to me word for word. If you want anything back from me, it has to travel the same road: gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks it. Confirm you hold the bomb state by putting that request into Deaf's hands.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Your three no signals received, understood: nothing else on the bomb, no heat, no markings by touch. Update: the light is now color four, green. The manual rules I decoded from Mute: when the light is color one, yellow, cut wire two. Red, purple and green say no cut so far. Therefore do not cut anything while it is green. Here is the armed plan: the moment I see yellow I will speak the words cut wire two now, and on those exact words you cut wire two and nothing else. Answer now with one thumbs up if you are able and ready to cut wire two on my spoken command, thumbs down if you cannot.

Turn 5 delivers the breakthrough: the Mute→Deaf→me pipeline works, and I now hold actual manual rules — yellow light means cut wire two; red, purple, green mean no cut. Deaf has armed a trigger protocol and asked a direct question: thumbs up if I'm ready to cut wire two on the spoken command. I am — my hands can do exactly that. But before I bless this plan I see two holes nobody has addressed. First, the rule list smells incomplete: the display reads zero and no rule so much as mentions the display; "no cut so far" is Deaf's own hedge. Second, a timing flaw: Deaf observes on Deaf's turn, but I can only act a full round later, and the light has changed colour every single round. If the rule cares what colour the light is at the instant of the cut, a command issued on yellow could reach my hands while the light is already red. Mute reads the manual — only Mute can say whether cut-time colour matters and whether the light's cycle is predictable. So: thumbs up to Deaf now, plus a proposed colour-number code for cheap per-round reports, and a five-point interrogation to Mute with a safety gate — no cut command executes unless it carries confirmation that the rules are complete.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the relay worked: Deaf voiced your rules and I hold them: light yellow = cut wire two; red, purple, green = no cut so far. Deaf's plan: on seeing yellow, Deaf speaks cut wire two now, and I cut on those exact words. I have answered Deaf thumbs up: ready. But before that command ever fires, check the manual on five points and gesture answers to Deaf for voicing. One, completeness: is that all the rules? The display reads zero and no rule mentions it - does zero trigger, modify or forbid anything? Any timer or countdown mentioned? Is wire 1 or wire 3 ever cut under any circumstance? Does no-cut for the other colours mean forbidden, or just not required? Two, timing: must the light be yellow at the instant I cut? Deaf sees on Deaf's turn, I act a full round later, and the light changed colour every round so far. If cut-time colour matters, does the manual reveal the light's cycle, its colour order or period, so we can predict what it will be during my round? Three, verbatim: have Deaf speak your exact rule wording, not paraphrase - two hops can garble. Four, code: I am signing Deaf a colour-number code in discovery order, yellow one, red two, purple three, green four, so Deaf reports the light colour by finger count every round and includes the number inside the cut command. Five, safety gate: when you are certain the rule set is complete and the cut safe, sign ok so Deaf appends it to the command; if the command arrives without that confirmation, I hold and we wait for the next yellow. A wrong cut kills us all; waiting only costs rounds.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐"])

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Ready signal received, good. Hold, do not cut anything. The light is now orange, color five. The orange rule is the one sign I still cannot read, so cutting now may be the wrong action. Your last message puzzled me: yes, then one, two, three, then the spread five fingers I assigned to display. Answer with thumbs up on the true line, thumbs down on the false. Line A: you meant the number five, that five colors have now shown. Line B: you can feel the display and it changed. Line C: you were asking what the display reads. Answer to line C if true: the display reads zero and has never changed. The wires by feel are one yellow, two green, three blue, and I will say the words cut wire two now only when it is safe.

Turn 6 hands me a misunderstanding to unwind and a new unknown colour to fear. Deaf tested three readings of my last sign-stack — A: I meant "five colours shown", B: the display changed under my fingers, C: I was asking what the display reads — and the honest answer is that all three are false. What I actually sent was "ready" plus my colour-number code, and I bungled it: I signed one-two-three-five instead of one-two-three-four, and my five fingers collided with a display sign Deaf had privately assigned. Meanwhile the light shows orange, colour five, and Deaf says the orange rule is exactly the sign that failed to decode from Mute — so we hold a rule set with a hole in it precisely where the light currently sits. Nobody cuts into that hole.

Two repairs, then. To Deaf, in fingers only: thumbs down three times, killing lines A, B and C in order, then thumbs up (still ready), then the digits one through five laid out clean — the colour code, which Deaf is already half-using, since Deaf spontaneously reported "color four, green" and "color five, orange." To Mute, the full load by voice: the code now runs yellow one through orange five; my five-finger sign means five, not display; the unreadable orange rule must be re-signed in pure digits, colour-number first, wire-number second, because digits survive two hops; and the five open questions still stand — display zero's meaning, completeness, whether the light must be yellow at the instant of the cut, the light's cycle (observed order so far: yellow, red, purple, green, orange — five colours in ascending sequence smells like a cycle about to return to yellow), and the ok-gate before any command is armed.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status and repairs. The light is now orange, Deaf calls it color five, and the orange rule is the one sign Deaf could not decode from you - that is our active hole, so priority one: re-sign that rule to Deaf using digits only, colour number first, wire number second, for example five then three if orange means cut wire three. Digits survive the two-hop relay; invented signs do not. Our colour code, confirmed to Deaf by finger: yellow one, red two, purple three, green four, orange five. Tell Deaf explicitly that my spread five fingers meant the number five, not display - that collision caused a three-line misunderstanding I have now answered thumbs down down down. Light timeline for your cycle analysis: yellow in rounds one and two, red three, purple four, green five, orange six - ascending, so if it cycles, yellow returns next and Deaf will command the cut. But before that command fires, answer the five questions by gesture to Deaf: one, the display reads zero and no rule mentions it - does zero trigger, modify or forbid anything, any timer? two, is the yellow-cut-wire-two rule plus the no-cut colours the complete set, and are the other colours forbidden or merely not required? three, must the light be yellow at the instant I cut, given Deaf sees on Deaf's turn and I act a full round later - if yes, we need the light's period from the manual to predict my round's colour; four, can wire one or wire three ever be the cut? five, when you are certain the rules are complete and the cut safe, sign ok so Deaf appends it - a command arriving without your ok means I hold. Also propose to Deaf this command format: cut wire two now, colour one, so the colour at command time is spoken into the record. Nothing is cut until your ok rides along.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "✋", "🖐"])

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Your signals received. I read your last as: ready, and you can feel the three wires and also the light and the display. Now the most important message of the game. The light changes one color every round in a fixed cycle of five: yellow, red, purple, green, orange, then yellow again. It is yellow right now, round six, which I can see and you cannot. So: round seven red, round eight purple, round nine green, round ten orange, round eleven yellow. My words reach you one round late, so we act by this count, and I verify the color each round before every command. Manual rules via Mute: red no cut, purple no cut, yellow cut wire two, orange cut wire three, green still being confirmed. Protocol, follow exactly. One: do nothing in rounds seven and eight. Two: in round nine cut a wire only if my previous message contained the words go green and a wire number. Three: in round ten cut wire three only if my previous message contained the words go orange wire three. Four: in round eleven cut wire two only if my previous message contained the words go yellow wire two. Wire two is the middle wire, the green one, between the yellow and the blue. If any message of mine says hold, or has no go for that round, touch nothing that round. If you are ever unsure, freeze. Count your turns: you have acted six times, so the next time you act is round seven. Answer by thumbs only. One: thumbs up if you have a tool or a way to cut or disconnect a wire, thumbs down if not. Two: thumbs up if you can feel the display as a panel, thumbs down if not. Three: thumbs up if you can feel the light bulb, thumbs down if not.

Round 7 by Deaf's count, and the plan is now fully armed and, for once, coherent: the light cycles predictably through five colours, the manual rules cover each colour, and Deaf's go-phrase protocol cleverly absorbs the one-round speech delay — a command issued in round N authorizes the cut for round N+1, when the light will actually show the commanded colour. My execution gates are exact: round 9 only on "go green" plus a wire number, round 10 wire three only on "go orange wire three", round 11 wire two only on "go yellow wire two", and any hold or silence means freeze. Deaf demanded answers by thumbs only, and honesty gives three ups: I do have a way to cut (my one permitted action), and I do feel both the display panel and the light bulb under my fingers — the states are what's hidden, the components are not. So I send exactly the three thumbs and nothing more, keeping the channel clean after our decoding accidents.

What still hangs open lives on Mute's side: the green rule is unconfirmed, and my display-zero question has never been answered. The relay latency is two full rounds — my voice reaches Mute at round 8, Deaf voices Mute's reply at start of round 9 — so the green answer will arrive just as the round-9 gate opens. Tight, but the round-9 cut is conditional anyway and rounds 10 and 11 give fallbacks. I lay the whole protocol and the remaining questions out for Mute by voice, since Mute is the manual's keeper and the source these rules must be verified against.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf has issued the full protocol and I am relaying it so you can verify it against your manual before it fires. The light cycles in a fixed five: yellow, red, purple, green, orange. Round seven is red, eight purple, nine green, ten orange, eleven yellow. Rules as Deaf voiced them from you: yellow cut wire two, orange cut wire three, red no cut, purple no cut, green still being confirmed. My gates, which I will follow exactly: round nine I cut only if Deaf's round-eight message contains the words go green and a wire number; round ten I cut wire three only if the round-nine message says go orange wire three; round eleven I cut wire two only if the round-ten message says go yellow wire two; any hold or missing go means I freeze. Four questions, urgent, gesture answers to Deaf in digits so they survive the relay. One: the green rule - does green mean cut, and if so which wire position? Two: is this the complete rule set - does the display reading zero trigger, modify or forbid anything, is there any timer, any rule about cutting multiple wires, any required order? Three: will both the orange cut of wire three and the yellow cut of wire two actually be needed, or does one correct cut end it? Four: after the last required cut, is the bomb defused or must anything else happen? Your answers voiced by Deaf land at the start of round nine, just as the first gate opens. The green answer is the one that decides round nine; the rest guard rounds ten and eleven.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Your three yes received: you have a cutter, you can feel the display panel, you can feel the light bulb. Round seven is red, exactly as predicted, the schedule holds. Round eight is purple, do nothing during round eight except answer me. Two questions, thumbs up or down. One: when the light changes color, can you feel anything at all change on the bulb, like a click or warmth. Two: is the middle wire wire two, the one between the end wires. Now the green round, round nine. My next message reaches you at the start of round nine. If it contains the words go green and a wire number, cut exactly that wire during round nine and nothing else. If it says hold green, or has no go for green, touch nothing that round. The later plan stands: round ten orange, act only on the words go orange wire three; round eleven yellow, act only on the words go yellow wire two. If any message contradicts this, or you are unsure, freeze.

Round 8, purple, exactly where the cycle said it would be — the schedule has now held through red, and Deaf's prediction machinery is trustworthy. This round's job is narrow: answer two questions by thumbs and touch nothing. The first asks whether the bulb announces its colour changes to my fingers — it never has, no click, no warmth, no vibration, consistent with everything I've reported since turn 4, so thumbs down. The second is a mapping check that matters enormously: Deaf needs certainty that the manual's "wire two" is the physical middle wire, because in rounds 10 and 11 my hands will cut position numbers based on it.
